stem.text: A potentiometer circuit is used to determine the electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$ of a cell. The circuit includes a second cell of e.m.f. $1.5\,\text{V}$ and internal resistance $0.50\,\Omega$ that is connected to a uniform resistance wire XY, as shown.

stem.alt: Potentiometer circuit with a second cell and resistor in a dashed outline, a uniform resistance wire from X to Y with a movable connection Z, and a cell labelled E, with length 0.64 m marked from X to Z and the wire labelled length 0.96 m and resistance 0.50 Ω

stem.text: The resistance wire XY has a length of $0.96\,\text{m}$ and a resistance of $0.50\,\Omega$.
The movable connection Z is moved along wire XY. The galvanometer reading is zero when length XZ is $0.64\,\text{m}$.
What is the value of e.m.f. $E$?
